samples.question: The picture shows five horizontal LANES of small upright tick marks: one red lane, one green, one blue, one orange and one purple. A lane is simply all the marks of one colour sitting on one grey rail. Every lane holds exactly the same number of marks, eight, every lane's leftmost mark starts at the same place on the page and every lane's rightmost mark ends at the same place, and every mark is drawn the same size and the same brightness. So the number of marks, the amount of coloured ink, how far a lane reaches, how wide a lane is and the average spacing of a lane are identical for all five colours and mean nothing. Take one lane at a time and look only at the seven GAPS between its neighbouring marks, measured from mark to mark along the page. Find that lane's WIDEST gap and that lane's NARROWEST gap and subtract the narrowest from the widest: that difference is how UNEVEN the lane is, and a lane whose marks are spaced almost equally gives a small difference. The answer is the colour of the lane with the SMALLEST such difference, that is, the most evenly spaced lane. No gap is marked, measured or labelled anywhere in the picture, and vertical height, the top-to-bottom order of the lanes and the left-to-right order of the marks mean nothing. Cheap readings are deliberately steered elsewhere: in every picture the lane holding the single widest gap of all, the lane holding the single narrowest gap of all and the lane with the widest opening gap each belong to a colour that is NOT the answer, and which row a lane occupies is the answer no more often than chance allows. The frame, the pale grey vertical guide lines and the grey rails are decoration and mean nothing. Which colour's lane is the most evenly spaced? Answer red, green, blue, orange or purple.
